images.title: Choosing the cut
images.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Project: Leafline. These are newly made concept/reference and store-page images, never in-game textures.
Shared art direction, reused from the initial set: grounded stylized realism with a painterly cinematic finish, attractive readable large shapes, credible macro-scale nature, warm brown bark and green leaves. Tree forms should feel feasible with procedural geometry and math/shader-driven surfaces: strong bark ridges and branching silhouettes, restrained microdetail.
Current design: summer canopy, warm plated bark with deep fissures and patches of moss, backlit green leaves. An ordinary full-sized tree is enormous beside a millimetre-long ant: broad bark plates and a trunk whose curvature disappears beyond the frame. Use the intimate close-to-bark perspective of a camera looking up a real trunk, with mild depth of field that preserves readable surfaces.
Leafcutter identity when present: dark reddish-brown Atta worker, large heart-shaped head, elbowed antennae, strong mandibles, small dorsal thorax spines, narrow TWO-SEGMENT waist, oval gaster, exactly six legs in three pairs from the thorax. Natural insect anatomy without human hands, faces or clothing.
Carrying rule when present: exactly one CUT leaf fragment gripped at its lower edge in the mandibles and held UPRIGHT ABOVE THE HEAD, a vertical sail catching light, never flat out in front, never a whole leaf on a stem, never in a backpack or on a pole.
Scent rule when present: a THIN restrained translucent cyan trace hugging the bark surface, subordinate to the environment, never a neon rope or raised rail.
Constraints: original art, no text at all, no lettering, logos, trademarks, watermarks or UI. No weapons, rockets, birds, injuries, animal harm, nest interior, villages or fantasy architecture. No collage or multi-panel board.
Asset type: gameplay concept and leaf-cutting reference. Output: one 3:2 landscape illustration.
Primary request: a close, clear view of a leafcutter making a half-finished curved cut in a living leaf, demonstrating the choice of fragment size.
Scene: a fine woody twig branches off a much larger limb; a backlit green leaf grows from a short petiole. The original leaf is roughly ten ant lengths long. A reddish-brown Atta worker stands with ALL SIX FEET ON THE WOODY TWIG beside the leaf's base, its head reaching the near lower edge of the blade. It is not standing or walking on the leaf itself.
Action: mandibles visibly meet a fresh half-circle incision at the near edge. The partly separated fragment remains connected by a clear uncut bridge. The intended curved piece is two or three ant lengths wide, sufficiently close to the base that the worker can cut while on the twig. Show the pale fresh cut edge, a subtle curl in the partly freed piece, branching veins, and a small older round bite elsewhere on the leaf. The shape must read as deliberate curved leaf cutting rather than random torn damage. There is no carried fragment yet.
Composition: three-quarter camera close enough to read mandibles, twig contact and the curved incision, with enough full ant silhouette to distinguish legs from antennae. A huge warm bark limb fades behind it. The leaf's luminous lamina provides a clean backdrop for the head and cut.
Lighting/mood: focused, tactile and calm, soft sunlight transmitted through green lamina, warm bark highlights. No floating risk gauge, colored diagram, cutting tools, labels or text.

Asset type: gameplay concept and wind/shelter reference. Output: one 3:2 landscape illustration.
Primary request: the same reddish-brown Atta worker as the cutting concept, now loaded with one large upright fragment, bracing against a directional gust on an exposed branch while a sheltered return route is visible.
Scene: an enormous branch curves into the main trunk, with a readable walkable bark saddle and a sheltered lee-side route wrapping around the massive trunk. The camera is behind and to the side of the ant at macro scale with a steady horizon.
Action: the controlled ant stops and grips, six legs spread and feet firmly anchored, body lowered. Its mandibles hold the lower edge of ONE cut leaf fragment UPRIGHT ABOVE ITS HEAD like a sail, about three ant lengths across. The vertical lamina visibly bows sideways in the gust; do not move it out in front or make the ant humanoid. Ant and leaf remain safe on the branch.
Wind design: a few fine translucent wind streaks flow consistently from the open side toward the trunk, background leaves and stems bend in the same direction, with one or two airborne leaf flecks. Wind streaks fade where the trunk shields the lee side. A thin cyan scent path wraps onto that calm sheltered side, visibly offering a safer route; keep it separate from the pale wind streaks.
Composition: exposed ant and bent sail in foreground, the huge trunk physically blocking the wind in the middle ground, a readable curved route into shelter. Enough depth to feel high above ground while keeping playable bark surfaces clear. No bird, falling injured ant, explosive storm effects or HUD.
Lighting/mood: warm-green summer daylight under a gust, tense and purposeful, with light still passing through the green sail.

images.title: Curved cut
images.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Art direction: grounded stylized realism with a painterly cinematic finish, attractive readable large shapes, credible macro-scale nature, warm brown bark and green leaves. Tree forms should feel feasible with procedural geometry and math/shader-driven surfaces: strong bark ridges and branching silhouettes, restrained microdetail. A recognizable dark reddish-brown worker ant has six legs, elbowed antennae, a segmented body and mandibles, with no human face, clothing or hands. The ant is millimetres long on an ordinary full-sized tree; preserve the enormous size difference. Scent paths, when requested, are a restrained translucent cyan gameplay visualization hugging the traversable surface, never a physical cable or magical beam.
Asset type: game concept reference for the leaf cutting shader and wind-risk indicator.
Primary request: At ant scale, one natural dark reddish-brown leafcutter worker stands securely on the twig at the base of a backlit broad summer leaf. Its mandibles are engaged with the accessible leaf edge beside the petiole, halfway through a curved cut that will remove a broad semicircular fragment. Show an unmistakable thin dark half-finished curved incision starting at the leaf edge, with the prospective fragment still attached along its uncut arc; no detached carried load yet. The ant cuts from the twig, not by standing on the leaf blade. Leaf veins remain clear. A restrained translucent cyan scent trail ends on the bark of the twig beneath its feet.
Composition/framing: one landscape 3:2 illustration, close enough to read mandibles, cut and veins, but keep bark and neighboring leaves large relative to the millimetre ant. No scissors or tools. Warm dappled daylight, backlit green tissue. A very subtle non-text gameplay guide hugs the intended cut, transitioning desaturated green near its start through amber to a tiny warm orange-red endpoint to suggest increasing wind risk with fragment area; no HUD panel, labels, arrows or symbols.
Constraints: No text, letters, numbers, glyphs, captions, logos, trademarks, watermarks or weapons anywhere. Natural leafcutter ant anatomy, six legs and two elbowed antennae. A carried fragment is gripped at its lower edge by the mandibles and stands UPRIGHT ABOVE THE HEAD like a broad vertical sail, never held out horizontally in front and never worn as a backpack. No clothing, human hands or humanoid insects. No birds. No collage.
